keywords: software, subscription, saas, license, annual, monthly, cloud, platform

Monthly amortization: Debit Subscription Expense (OPEX), Credit Prepaid Expenses. Example: A 12-month software license for $2,400 creates $200/month expense.

keywords: laptop, computer, server, equipment, hardware, machinery, furniture, vehicle, asset
rule: An item must be capitalized (treated as CAPEX) when it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity AND the cost can be measured reliably AND the useful life exceeds one accounting period (typically 1 year). Computers, laptops, servers, and equipment with useful life over 1 year must be capitalized. Journal entry: Debit Computer Equipment / Fixed Assets (CAPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. Depreciation is then recorded over the useful life.

keywords: consulting, advisory, professional services, strategy, management consulting, advisory fee, professional fees
rule: Consulting services, professional fees, and advisory fees received and paid by the entity are operating expenses recognized when services are rendered. Journal entry: Debit Professional Services Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. These are NEVER classified under ASC 606 or IFRS 15 - those standards govern revenue recognition for the party delivering services, not the party receiving and paying for them.

keywords: rent, lease, office space, premises, facility, building, coworking, workspace
rule: Short-term lease payments (lease term 12 months or less) or low-value asset leases are expensed as incurred under IFRS 16 simplified approach. Journal entry: Debit Rent Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. Long-term leases (over 12 months) require right-of-use asset recognition: Debit Right-of-Use Asset, Credit Lease Liability.

Keywords: rent, lease, office space, premises, facility, building, coworking, workspace

keywords: marketing, advertising, promotion, campaign, social media, digital marketing, branding, PR
rule: Marketing, advertising, and promotional expenses are expensed as incurred. They do not meet the criteria for intangible asset recognition as future benefits are uncertain and cannot be reliably measured. Journal entry: Debit Marketing Expense / Advertising Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable.

Journal entry: Debit Marketing Expense / Advertising Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable.
Keywords: marketing, advertising, promotion, campaign, social media, digital marketing, branding, PR

keywords: travel, flight, hotel, accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxi, transport, conference
rule: Travel expenses for business purposes are expensed as incurred in the period the travel occurs. Journal entry: Debit Travel Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable or Employee Expense Payable. Entertainment expenses require documentation of business purpose. Meals are typically 50% deductible for tax purposes but fully expensed for accounting purposes.
text:

Entertainment expenses require documentation of business purpose. Meals are typically 50% deductible for tax purposes but fully expensed for accounting purposes.
Keywords: travel, flight, hotel, accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxi, transport, conference

keywords: research, development, R&D, prototype, feasibility study, innovation, testing
rule: Research costs must always be expensed as incurred - they cannot be capitalized. Development costs may be capitalized only when technical feasibility, intention to complete, ability to use or sell, and reliable measurement are all demonstrated. Journal entry for research: Debit R&D Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable.

keywords: electricity, utilities, internet, broadband, telephone, water, gas, telecoms, wifi
rule: Utility expenses including electricity, water, internet, and telecommunications are operating expenses incurred in the period of use. Journal entry: Debit Utilities Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. These are never capitalized.

keywords: training, education, course, certification, workshop, seminar, conference registration, learning
rule: Employee training, development, and education costs are expensed as incurred. They cannot be capitalized as intangible assets because the company does not control the future economic benefits (employee could leave). Journal entry: Debit Training Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable.
text:

Keywords: training, education, course, certification, workshop, seminar, conference registration, learning

keywords: software development, custom software, implementation, system integration, ERP, CRM, development hours
rule: Internal-use software development costs during the application development stage are capitalized. Preliminary project stage and post-implementation stage costs are expensed. Keywords: software development, custom software, implementation, system integration, ERP, CRM, development hours

keywords: maintenance, support, annual support, warranty, service contract, helpdesk, technical support
rule: Annual maintenance and support contracts for software or equipment are recognized ratably over the contract period, similar to subscriptions. If the maintenance period spans multiple accounting periods, the prepaid portion is deferred. Journal entry: Debit Prepaid Maintenance, Credit Accounts Payable. Monthly: Debit Maintenance Expense, Credit Prepaid Maintenance.

Keywords: maintenance, support, annual support, warranty, service contract, helpdesk, technical support

keywords: inventory, stock, goods, raw materials, components, parts, resale, manufacturing, merchandise
rule: Goods purchased for resale or for use in production are recorded as inventory (asset) not as expense. Journal entry: Debit Inventory (Asset), Credit Accounts Payable. The inventory is expensed as Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) when the goods are sold. Raw materials for manufacturing follow the same treatment.

Keywords: inventory, stock, goods, raw materials, components, parts, resale, manufacturing, merchandise

keywords: interest, finance charge, bank fee, loan fee, borrowing cost, credit facility
rule: Interest expense on borrowings and finance charges are expensed in the period incurred. They are not capitalized unless directly attributable to the acquisition of a qualifying asset under IAS 23. Journal entry: Debit Interest Expense (Finance Cost), Credit Accounts Payable or Accrued Interest.

Journal entry: Debit Interest Expense (Finance Cost), Credit Accounts Payable or Accrued Interest.
Keywords: interest, finance charge, bank fee, loan fee, borrowing cost, credit facility

keywords: recruitment, staffing, agency, headhunter, hiring fee, placement fee, temp agency
rule: Recruitment fees paid to staffing agencies for hiring permanent employees are expensed as incurred as they represent the cost of the recruitment service already rendered. Journal entry: Debit Recruitment Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. They are not capitalized as part of employee cost.

Keywords: recruitment, staffing, agency, headhunter, hiring fee, placement fee, temp agency

keywords: insurance, premium, indemnity, liability insurance, professional indemnity, cyber insurance, coverage
rule: Insurance premiums covering future periods are initially recorded as prepaid assets and expensed ratably over the coverage period. Journal entry on payment: Debit Prepaid Insurance (Asset), Credit Accounts Payable. Monthly: Debit Insurance Expense, Credit Prepaid Insurance.

Keywords: insurance, premium, indemnity, liability insurance, professional indemnity, cyber insurance, coverage

keywords: printing, reproduction, copying, brochure, flyer, banner, signage, print run
rule: Printing, copying, and document reproduction services used in operations are operating expenses incurred in the period. Journal entry: Debit Printing and Stationery Expense (OPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. Large print runs for marketing may be classified under Marketing Expense.
text:

keywords: vehicle, car, van, fleet, automobile, truck, lease vehicle, company car

Leased vehicles under IFRS 16 require right-of-use asset recognition for leases over 12 months.
text:

Leased vehicles under IFRS 16 require right-of-use asset recognition for leases over 12 months.
Keywords: vehicle, car, van, fleet, automobile, truck, lease vehicle, company car

keywords: freight, shipping, delivery, courier, logistics, DHL, FedEx, UPS, postage, dispatch

Keywords: freight, shipping, delivery, courier, logistics, DHL, FedEx, UPS, postage, dispatch

keywords: rug, carpet, furniture, furnishings, fixtures, fittings, decorative, art, painting

Journal entry: Debit Furniture and Fittings (CAPEX), Credit Accounts Payable. Low-value items below the capitalization threshold ($500-$2,500 depending on company policy) are expensed as Office Supplies Expense or Sundry Expenses.

topic: Revenue Over Time vs Point in Time
keywords: over time, point in time, milestone, progress, control transfer, customer acceptance
rule: Revenue is recognized over time if the customer receives and consumes benefits as performed, controls the asset as created, or the asset has no alternative use and there is an enforceable right to payment. Otherwise recognize at a point in time when control transfers.

Rule: Revenue is recognized over time if the customer receives and consumes benefits as performed, controls the asset as created, or the asset has no alternative use and there is an enforceable right to payment. Otherwise recognize at a point in time when control transfers.
Keywords: over time, point in time, milestone, progress, control transfer, customer acceptance

keywords: deferred revenue, contract asset, unbilled revenue, unearned revenue, advance billing, contract liability

Keywords: rebate, discount, refund, return, credit note, variable consideration, SLA credit, penalty

keywords: principal, agent, gross revenue, net revenue, marketplace, reseller, pass through, commission

keywords: sales commission, contract cost, deferred commission, fulfillment cost, onboarding, customer acquisition cost
rule: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract, such as recoverable sales commissions, are capitalized unless the amortization period is one year or less and practical expedient is elected. Fulfillment costs are capitalized only if they relate directly to a contract, generate resources used to satisfy obligations, and are expected to be recovered.
text:
Standard: ASC 340-40 / IFRS 15, Paragraph: ASC 340-40-25 / IFRS 15.91-98, Topic: Contract Costs - Sales Commissions and Fulfillment Costs
Rule: Incremental costs of obtaining a contract, such as recoverable sales commissions, are capitalized unless the amortization period is one year or less and practical expedient is elected. Fulfillment costs are capitalized only if they relate directly to a contract, generate resources used to satisfy obligations, and are expected to be recovered.
Keywords: sales commission, contract cost, deferred commission, fulfillment cost, onboarding, customer acquisition cost

keywords: inventory, stock, raw materials, finished goods, landed cost, freight-in, COGS
rule: Inventory cost includes purchase price, import duties, non-refundable taxes, freight-in, handling, conversion costs, and costs directly attributable to bringing inventory to present location and condition. Inventory is expensed as COGS when sold.
text:
Standard: IAS 2 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 2.10-18 / ASC 330-10, Topic: Inventory Cost Components
Rule: Inventory cost includes purchase price, import duties, non-refundable taxes, freight-in, handling, conversion costs, and costs directly attributable to bringing inventory to present location and condition. Inventory is expensed as COGS when sold.
Keywords: inventory, stock, raw materials, finished goods, landed cost, freight-in, COGS

topic: Inventory Net Realizable Value and Obsolescence
keywords: obsolete inventory, NRV, write-down, slow moving, damaged goods, excess stock, reserve
rule: Inventory is written down when cost is not recoverable due to damage, obsolescence, slow movement, declining selling prices, or excess stock. IFRS uses lower of cost and net realizable value; US GAAP treatment depends on inventory method.
text:
Standard: IAS 2 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 2.28-33 / ASC 330-10-35, Topic: Inventory Net Realizable Value and Obsolescence
Rule: Inventory is written down when cost is not recoverable due to damage, obsolescence, slow movement, declining selling prices, or excess stock. IFRS uses lower of cost and net realizable value; US GAAP treatment depends on inventory method.
Keywords: obsolete inventory, NRV, write-down, slow moving, damaged goods, excess stock, reserve

topic: Abnormal Waste, Storage, and Production Inefficiency
keywords: scrap, spoilage, abnormal waste, rework, storage, idle capacity, production variance
rule: Abnormal waste, excessive spoilage, avoidable rework, idle capacity costs, and storage not necessary for production are expensed as incurred rather than included in inventory.
text:
Standard: IAS 2 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 2.16 / ASC 330-10, Topic: Abnormal Waste, Storage, and Production Inefficiency
Rule: Abnormal waste, excessive spoilage, avoidable rework, idle capacity costs, and storage not necessary for production are expensed as incurred rather than included in inventory.
Keywords: scrap, spoilage, abnormal waste, rework, storage, idle capacity, production variance

keywords: FIFO, LIFO, weighted average, specific identification, inventory costing, cost flow
rule: Inventory cost flow assumptions must be applied consistently. IFRS permits FIFO and weighted average but prohibits LIFO. US GAAP permits FIFO, weighted average, specific identification, and LIFO when elected.
text:
Standard: IAS 2 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 2.25 / ASC 330-10, Topic: Inventory Costing Methods
Rule: Inventory cost flow assumptions must be applied consistently. IFRS permits FIFO and weighted average but prohibits LIFO. US GAAP permits FIFO, weighted average, specific identification, and LIFO when elected.
Keywords: FIFO, LIFO, weighted average, specific identification, inventory costing, cost flow

keywords: interest, borrowing cost, capitalized interest, qualifying asset, construction, loan, finance charge
rule: Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing, or producing a qualifying asset are capitalized while the asset is being prepared for intended use or sale. Other interest costs are expensed as incurred.
text:
Standard: IAS 23 / ASC 835-20, Paragraph: IAS 23.8 / ASC 835-20, Topic: Borrowing Costs Capitalization
Rule: Borrowing costs directly attributable to acquiring, constructing, or producing a qualifying asset are capitalized while the asset is being prepared for intended use or sale. Other interest costs are expensed as incurred.
Keywords: interest, borrowing cost, capitalized interest, qualifying asset, construction, loan, finance charge

keywords: impairment, recoverable amount, fair value, value in use, CGU, long-lived asset
rule: Assets are tested for impairment when indicators exist. IFRS compares carrying amount to recoverable amount. US GAAP long-lived assets held and used first use an undiscounted cash flow recoverability test, then fair value measurement if not recoverable.
text:
Standard: IAS 36 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 36.9-12 / ASC 360-10-35, Topic: Impairment of Long-Lived Assets
Rule: Assets are tested for impairment when indicators exist. IFRS compares carrying amount to recoverable amount. US GAAP long-lived assets held and used first use an undiscounted cash flow recoverability test, then fair value measurement if not recoverable.
Keywords: impairment, recoverable amount, fair value, value in use, CGU, long-lived asset

keywords: goodwill, impairment, acquisition, CGU, reporting unit, purchase price allocation
rule: Goodwill is not amortized under IFRS or US GAAP. It is tested for impairment annually and when indicators exist. Goodwill is allocated to CGUs under IFRS or reporting units under US GAAP.
text:
Standard: IAS 36 / ASC 350, Paragraph: IAS 36.90 / ASC 350-20, Topic: Goodwill Impairment
Rule: Goodwill is not amortized under IFRS or US GAAP. It is tested for impairment annually and when indicators exist. Goodwill is allocated to CGUs under IFRS or reporting units under US GAAP.
Keywords: goodwill, impairment, acquisition, CGU, reporting unit, purchase price allocation

keywords: acquisition, business combination, goodwill, PPA, due diligence, transaction costs
rule: In a business combination, identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recognized at acquisition-date fair value, with goodwill or bargain purchase gain for the difference. Acquisition-related transaction costs are generally expensed, not included in consideration transferred.
text:
Standard: IFRS 3 / ASC 805, Paragraph: IFRS 3.10-19 / ASC 805-20, Topic: Business Combination and Acquisition Accounting
Rule: In a business combination, identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recognized at acquisition-date fair value, with goodwill or bargain purchase gain for the difference. Acquisition-related transaction costs are generally expensed, not included in consideration transferred.
Keywords: acquisition, business combination, goodwill, PPA, due diligence, transaction costs

keywords: provision, contingency, legal claim, lawsuit, probable, estimate, accrued liability
rule: Recognize a provision when there is a present obligation from a past event, outflow is probable, and amount can be reliably estimated. Under US GAAP, loss contingencies are accrued when probable and reasonably estimable. Possible obligations are disclosed but not recognized.
text:
Standard: IAS 37 / ASC 450, Paragraph: IAS 37.14 / ASC 450-20, Topic: Provisions and Contingent Liabilities
Rule: Recognize a provision when there is a present obligation from a past event, outflow is probable, and amount can be reliably estimated. Under US GAAP, loss contingencies are accrued when probable and reasonably estimable. Possible obligations are disclosed but not recognized.
Keywords: provision, contingency, legal claim, lawsuit, probable, estimate, accrued liability

keywords: warranty, guarantee, service plan, assurance warranty, extended warranty, repair obligation
rule: Assurance-type warranties are accrued when the related sale occurs based on expected costs. Service-type warranties are separate performance obligations and revenue is deferred and recognized over the service period.
text:
Standard: IAS 37 / ASC 460 / ASC 606, Paragraph: IAS 37.24 / ASC 606-10-55, Topic: Warranty Obligations
Rule: Assurance-type warranties are accrued when the related sale occurs based on expected costs. Service-type warranties are separate performance obligations and revenue is deferred and recognized over the service period.
Keywords: warranty, guarantee, service plan, assurance warranty, extended warranty, repair obligation

topic: Payroll, Bonuses, Commissions, and Vacation Accruals
keywords: payroll, salary, wages, bonus, commission, vacation, holiday pay, employee, payroll tax
rule: Wages, salaries, bonuses, commissions, vacation pay, and payroll taxes are accrued when employees render service, even if paid later. Accumulating compensated absences are accrued when earned if criteria are met.
text:
Standard: IAS 19 / ASC 710, Paragraph: IAS 19.11 / ASC 710-10, Topic: Payroll, Bonuses, Commissions, and Vacation Accruals
Rule: Wages, salaries, bonuses, commissions, vacation pay, and payroll taxes are accrued when employees render service, even if paid later. Accumulating compensated absences are accrued when earned if criteria are met.
Keywords: payroll, salary, wages, bonus, commission, vacation, holiday pay, employee, payroll tax

keywords: pension, retirement, defined benefit, defined contribution, actuarial, post-employment
rule: Defined contribution plans are expensed as contributions become payable. Defined benefit plans require actuarial measurement of obligation and plan assets, with service cost, interest cost, remeasurements, and disclosures under applicable standards.
text:
Standard: IAS 19 / ASC 715, Paragraph: IAS 19.57 / ASC 715-30, Topic: Pension and Post-Employment Benefits
Rule: Defined contribution plans are expensed as contributions become payable. Defined benefit plans require actuarial measurement of obligation and plan assets, with service cost, interest cost, remeasurements, and disclosures under applicable standards.
Keywords: pension, retirement, defined benefit, defined contribution, actuarial, post-employment

keywords: stock option, RSU, share based compensation, equity award, vesting, grant date
rule: Equity-settled share-based awards are measured at grant-date fair value and expensed over the vesting period. Liability-classified awards are remeasured until settlement. Forfeitures, modifications, and performance conditions must be evaluated.
text:
Standard: IFRS 2 / ASC 718, Paragraph: 718-10-50, Topic: Share-Based Compensation
Rule: Equity-settled share-based awards are measured at grant-date fair value and expensed over the vesting period. Liability-classified awards are remeasured until settlement. Forfeitures, modifications, and performance conditions must be evaluated.
Keywords: stock option, RSU, share based compensation, equity award, vesting, grant date

keywords: income tax, corporate tax, deferred tax, tax payable, DTA, DTL, valuation allowance
rule: Current tax is recognized for taxes payable or recoverable for the period. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for temporary differences between accounting carrying amounts and tax bases, subject to recoverability or valuation allowance assessment.
text:
Standard: IAS 12 / ASC 740, Paragraph: IAS 12.15-24 / ASC 740-10, Topic: Income Taxes - Current and Deferred
Rule: Current tax is recognized for taxes payable or recoverable for the period. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for temporary differences between accounting carrying amounts and tax bases, subject to recoverability or valuation allowance assessment.
Keywords: income tax, corporate tax, deferred tax, tax payable, DTA, DTL, valuation allowance

keywords: VAT, GST, sales tax, input tax, output tax, tax code, reverse charge
rule: VAT, GST, and sales tax collected from customers or paid to vendors are usually recorded as tax receivable or payable when the company acts as tax collector, not as revenue or expense. Non-recoverable taxes are included in asset cost or expense depending on the underlying item.
text:
Standard: IAS 12 / ASC 740, Paragraph: IAS 12.46 / ASC 740-10, Topic: Sales Tax, VAT, and GST
Rule: VAT, GST, and sales tax collected from customers or paid to vendors are usually recorded as tax receivable or payable when the company acts as tax collector, not as revenue or expense. Non-recoverable taxes are included in asset cost or expense depending on the underlying item.
Keywords: VAT, GST, sales tax, input tax, output tax, tax code, reverse charge

keywords: foreign currency, FX, exchange rate, revaluation, translation, EUR, USD, GBP
rule: Foreign currency transactions are initially recorded at the spot rate on transaction date. Monetary balances are retranslated at closing rates at reporting date, with exchange differences recognized in profit or loss unless hedge or net investment rules apply.
text:
Standard: IAS 21 / ASC 830, Paragraph: IAS 21.21-28 / ASC 830-20, Topic: Foreign Currency Transactions
Rule: Foreign currency transactions are initially recorded at the spot rate on transaction date. Monetary balances are retranslated at closing rates at reporting date, with exchange differences recognized in profit or loss unless hedge or net investment rules apply.
Keywords: foreign currency, FX, exchange rate, revaluation, translation, EUR, USD, GBP

keywords: bad debt, allowance, expected credit loss, ECL, CECL, doubtful accounts, aging
rule: Receivables must be evaluated for expected credit losses. IFRS uses expected credit loss model, often lifetime ECL for trade receivables. US GAAP uses CECL for financial assets measured at amortized cost.
text:
Standard: IFRS 9 / ASC 326, Paragraph: IFRS 9.5.5 / ASC 326-20, Topic: Accounts Receivable Credit Losses
Rule: Receivables must be evaluated for expected credit losses. IFRS uses expected credit loss model, often lifetime ECL for trade receivables. US GAAP uses CECL for financial assets measured at amortized cost.
Keywords: bad debt, allowance, expected credit loss, ECL, CECL, doubtful accounts, aging

keywords: derivative, hedge, forward, swap, option, fair value, FX forward, cash flow hedge
rule: Derivatives are recognized on balance sheet at fair value. Hedge accounting is allowed only when documentation, eligibility, and effectiveness requirements are met. Otherwise fair value changes generally go to profit or loss.
text:
Standard: IFRS 9 / ASC 815, Paragraph: IFRS 9.6 / ASC 815-20, Topic: Derivatives and Hedge Accounting
Rule: Derivatives are recognized on balance sheet at fair value. Hedge accounting is allowed only when documentation, eligibility, and effectiveness requirements are met. Otherwise fair value changes generally go to profit or loss.
Keywords: derivative, hedge, forward, swap, option, fair value, FX forward, cash flow hedge

topic: Debt, Loans, and Effective Interest Method
keywords: debt, loan, borrowing, note payable, interest, covenant, effective interest, debt issuance costs
rule: Debt is initially recognized at fair value net of eligible transaction costs and subsequently measured using the effective interest method unless measured at fair value. Debt issuance costs are generally deferred and amortized over the debt term.
text:
Standard: IFRS 9 / ASC 470, Paragraph: IFRS 9.5.4 / ASC 835-30, Topic: Debt, Loans, and Effective Interest Method
Rule: Debt is initially recognized at fair value net of eligible transaction costs and subsequently measured using the effective interest method unless measured at fair value. Debt issuance costs are generally deferred and amortized over the debt term.
Keywords: debt, loan, borrowing, note payable, interest, covenant, effective interest, debt issuance costs

keywords: equity, liability, preferred shares, convertible, redemption, warrant, fixed for fixed
rule: Financial instruments are classified as liabilities or equity based on contractual obligations. An obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset generally creates a liability. Fixed-for-fixed equity settlement may support equity classification under IFRS subject to detailed rules.
text:
Standard: IAS 32 / ASC 480, Paragraph: IAS 32.15-32 / ASC 480-10, Topic: Liability vs Equity Classification
Rule: Financial instruments are classified as liabilities or equity based on contractual obligations. An obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset generally creates a liability. Fixed-for-fixed equity settlement may support equity classification under IFRS subject to detailed rules.
Keywords: equity, liability, preferred shares, convertible, redemption, warrant, fixed for fixed

keywords: cash flow, operating, investing, financing, statement of cash flows, noncash
rule: Cash flows are classified as operating, investing, or financing based on nature. IFRS permits some policy choices for interest and dividends; US GAAP is more prescriptive.
text:
Standard: IAS 7 / ASC 230, Paragraph: IAS 7.10 / ASC 230-10, Topic: Cash Flow Statement Classification
Rule: Cash flows are classified as operating, investing, or financing based on nature. IFRS permits some policy choices for interest and dividends; US GAAP is more prescriptive.
Keywords: cash flow, operating, investing, financing, statement of cash flows, noncash

topic: Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Restricted Cash
keywords: cash, cash equivalent, bank, deposit, money market, treasury bill, restricted cash, overdraft
rule: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known cash amounts and subject to insignificant value-change risk, typically original maturities of three months or less. Restricted cash must be separately tracked and disclosed.
text:
Standard: IAS 7 / ASC 305, Paragraph: IAS 7.6-8 / ASC 305-10, Topic: Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Restricted Cash
Rule: Cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid investments readily convertible to known cash amounts and subject to insignificant value-change risk, typically original maturities of three months or less. Restricted cash must be separately tracked and disclosed.
Keywords: cash, cash equivalent, bank, deposit, money market, treasury bill, restricted cash, overdraft

keywords: subsequent event, after reporting period, adjusting event, non-adjusting, disclosure, year end
rule: Adjusting subsequent events provide evidence of conditions existing at reporting date and require adjustment. Non-adjusting events relate to conditions arising after reporting date and generally require disclosure if material.
text:
Standard: IAS 10 / ASC 855, Paragraph: IAS 10.3-10 / ASC 855-10, Topic: Events After Reporting Period
Rule: Adjusting subsequent events provide evidence of conditions existing at reporting date and require adjustment. Non-adjusting events relate to conditions arising after reporting date and generally require disclosure if material.
Keywords: subsequent event, after reporting period, adjusting event, non-adjusting, disclosure, year end

keywords: estimate, error, prior period adjustment, restatement, accounting policy, retrospective, prospective
rule: Changes in accounting estimates are applied prospectively. Prior period errors are corrected retrospectively when material. Changes in accounting policy are applied retrospectively unless impracticable or transitional guidance says otherwise.
text:
Standard: IAS 8 / ASC 250, Paragraph: IAS 8.5 / ASC 250-10, Topic: Accounting Estimates vs Errors
Rule: Changes in accounting estimates are applied prospectively. Prior period errors are corrected retrospectively when material. Changes in accounting policy are applied retrospectively unless impracticable or transitional guidance says otherwise.
Keywords: estimate, error, prior period adjustment, restatement, accounting policy, retrospective, prospective

keywords: related party, affiliate, director, shareholder, owner, family, management, arm's length
rule: Related party relationships, transactions, balances, commitments, and key management compensation require identification and disclosure. Transactions should be assessed for arm's-length terms and proper authorization.
text:
Standard: IAS 24 / ASC 850, Paragraph: IAS 24.9-18 / ASC 850-10, Topic: Related Party Transactions
Rule: Related party relationships, transactions, balances, commitments, and key management compensation require identification and disclosure. Transactions should be assessed for arm's-length terms and proper authorization.
Keywords: related party, affiliate, director, shareholder, owner, family, management, arm's length

keywords: consolidation, control, subsidiary, VIE, structured entity, noncontrolling interest, group
rule: Consolidate entities controlled by the reporting entity. IFRS control requires power over investee, exposure to variable returns, and ability to use power to affect returns. US GAAP uses voting interest and variable interest entity models.
text:
Standard: IFRS 10 / ASC 810, Paragraph: IFRS 10.7 / ASC 810-10, Topic: Consolidation and Control
Rule: Consolidate entities controlled by the reporting entity. IFRS control requires power over investee, exposure to variable returns, and ability to use power to affect returns. US GAAP uses voting interest and variable interest entity models.
Keywords: consolidation, control, subsidiary, VIE, structured entity, noncontrolling interest, group

keywords: intercompany, elimination, group, parent, subsidiary, IC receivable, IC payable, transfer pricing
rule: Intercompany receivables, payables, revenue, expenses, dividends, loans, and unrealized profits in inventory or fixed assets are eliminated in consolidation.
text:
Standard: IFRS 10 / ASC 810, Paragraph: IFRS 10.B86 / ASC 810-10, Topic: Intercompany Eliminations
Rule: Intercompany receivables, payables, revenue, expenses, dividends, loans, and unrealized profits in inventory or fixed assets are eliminated in consolidation.
Keywords: intercompany, elimination, group, parent, subsidiary, IC receivable, IC payable, transfer pricing

keywords: associate, equity method, significant influence, investment, share of profit, dividend
rule: Investments with significant influence, generally presumed at 20 percent or more voting power unless rebutted, are accounted for using the equity method. The investor recognizes its share of investee profit or loss and adjusts the investment carrying amount.
text:
Standard: IAS 28 / ASC 323, Paragraph: IAS 28.3 / ASC 323-10, Topic: Equity Method Investments
Rule: Investments with significant influence, generally presumed at 20 percent or more voting power unless rebutted, are accounted for using the equity method. The investor recognizes its share of investee profit or loss and adjusts the investment carrying amount.
Keywords: associate, equity method, significant influence, investment, share of profit, dividend

keywords: government grant, subsidy, incentive, aid, grant income, deferred grant, reimbursement
rule: Government grants are recognized when there is reasonable assurance that conditions will be met and grant will be received. Income grants are recognized systematically with related costs. Asset grants under IFRS are deferred or deducted from asset carrying amount depending on policy.
text:
Standard: IAS 20 / ASC 958 / ASC 450, Paragraph: IAS 20.7-12, Topic: Government Grants and Incentives
Rule: Government grants are recognized when there is reasonable assurance that conditions will be met and grant will be received. Income grants are recognized systematically with related costs. Asset grants under IFRS are deferred or deducted from asset carrying amount depending on policy.
Keywords: government grant, subsidy, incentive, aid, grant income, deferred grant, reimbursement

keywords: investment property, rental property, capital appreciation, real estate, fair value model
rule: Under IFRS, property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation is investment property and accounted for using fair value or cost model policy. Under US GAAP, investment property generally follows property guidance unless industry-specific rules apply.
text:
Standard: IAS 40 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 40.5 / ASC 360-10, Topic: Investment Property
Rule: Under IFRS, property held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation is investment property and accounted for using fair value or cost model policy. Under US GAAP, investment property generally follows property guidance unless industry-specific rules apply.
Keywords: investment property, rental property, capital appreciation, real estate, fair value model

keywords: depreciation, useful life, accumulated depreciation, straight line, asset register, in service
rule: Depreciable assets are depreciated over useful lives from the date available for intended use. Depreciation method should reflect consumption pattern and be reviewed periodically. Land is generally not depreciated.
text:
Standard: IAS 16 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 16.30-31 / ASC 360-10, Topic: Depreciation of Fixed Assets
Rule: Depreciable assets are depreciated over useful lives from the date available for intended use. Depreciation method should reflect consumption pattern and be reviewed periodically. Land is generally not depreciated.
Keywords: depreciation, useful life, accumulated depreciation, straight line, asset register, in service

keywords: disposal, sale of asset, scrap, retirement, write off, gain on disposal, loss on disposal
rule: When a fixed asset is sold, scrapped, or retired, remove cost and accumulated depreciation and recognize gain or loss based on proceeds compared with carrying amount.
text:
Standard: IAS 16 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 16.67-72 / ASC 360-10, Topic: Fixed Asset Disposals
Rule: When a fixed asset is sold, scrapped, or retired, remove cost and accumulated depreciation and recognize gain or loss based on proceeds compared with carrying amount.
Keywords: disposal, sale of asset, scrap, retirement, write off, gain on disposal, loss on disposal

keywords: installation, delivery, site preparation, testing, commissioning, directly attributable, asset cost
rule: PPE cost includes purchase price and directly attributable costs needed to bring asset to location and condition for intended use, such as delivery, installation, site preparation, testing, and professional fees. General administration, training, and maintenance are expensed.
text:
Standard: IAS 16 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 16.16-17 / ASC 360-10, Topic: Directly Attributable Asset Costs
Rule: PPE cost includes purchase price and directly attributable costs needed to bring asset to location and condition for intended use, such as delivery, installation, site preparation, testing, and professional fees. General administration, training, and maintenance are expensed.
Keywords: installation, delivery, site preparation, testing, commissioning, directly attributable, asset cost

keywords: construction in progress, CIP, project cost, build out, construction, in service, capitalization
rule: Costs incurred to construct or develop a fixed asset before it is ready for use are recorded as construction in progress. Depreciation begins when asset is available for intended use, not necessarily when it generates revenue.
text:
Standard: IAS 16 / ASC 360, Paragraph: IAS 16.73 / ASC 360-10, Topic: Construction in Progress
Rule: Costs incurred to construct or develop a fixed asset before it is ready for use are recorded as construction in progress. Depreciation begins when asset is available for intended use, not necessarily when it generates revenue.
Keywords: construction in progress, CIP, project cost, build out, construction, in service, capitalization

keywords: leasehold improvement, tenant improvement, buildout, renovation, fit out, landlord incentive
rule: Improvements to leased property are capitalized if asset criteria are met and cost exceeds threshold. Depreciate over shorter of useful life and lease term unless ownership transfers or renewal is reasonably certain.
text:
Standard: IFRS 16 / IAS 16 / ASC 842, Paragraph: 16.16, Topic: Leasehold Improvements
Rule: Improvements to leased property are capitalized if asset criteria are met and cost exceeds threshold. Depreciate over shorter of useful life and lease term unless ownership transfers or renewal is reasonably certain.
Keywords: leasehold improvement, tenant improvement, buildout, renovation, fit out, landlord incentive

topic: Asset Retirement Obligations and Restoration Costs
keywords: asset retirement obligation, ARO, restoration, decommissioning, dismantling, make good
rule: Obligations to dismantle, remove, or restore assets or leased sites are recognized when a present obligation exists and can be estimated. Initial obligation is usually capitalized as part of related asset and depreciated, with liability accretion over time.
text:
Standard: IAS 37 / ASC 410, Paragraph: 21-410-20, Topic: Asset Retirement Obligations and Restoration Costs
Rule: Obligations to dismantle, remove, or restore assets or leased sites are recognized when a present obligation exists and can be estimated. Initial obligation is usually capitalized as part of related asset and depreciated, with liability accretion over time.
Keywords: asset retirement obligation, ARO, restoration, decommissioning, dismantling, make good

keywords: intangible, patent, trademark, license, customer relationship, technology, amortization
rule: An acquired intangible asset is recognized when identifiable, controlled by the entity, future benefits are probable, and cost or fair value can be measured reliably. Finite-lived intangibles are amortized; indefinite-lived intangibles are not amortized but tested for impairment.
text:
Standard: IAS 38 / ASC 350, Paragraph: IAS 38.21 / ASC 350-30, Topic: Acquired Intangible Assets
Rule: An acquired intangible asset is recognized when identifiable, controlled by the entity, future benefits are probable, and cost or fair value can be measured reliably. Finite-lived intangibles are amortized; indefinite-lived intangibles are not amortized but tested for impairment.
Keywords: intangible, patent, trademark, license, customer relationship, technology, amortization

topic: Internally Generated Brands and Customer Lists
keywords: brand, trademark, customer list, masthead, publishing title, internally generated intangible
rule: Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists, and similar items are not recognized as intangible assets because cost cannot be distinguished reliably from business development as a whole. Acquired identifiable intangibles may be recognized.
text:
Standard: IAS 38 / ASC 350, Paragraph: IAS 38.63 / ASC 350-30, Topic: Internally Generated Brands and Customer Lists
Rule: Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists, and similar items are not recognized as intangible assets because cost cannot be distinguished reliably from business development as a whole. Acquired identifiable intangibles may be recognized.
Keywords: brand, trademark, customer list, masthead, publishing title, internally generated intangible

keywords: website, web development, hosting, domain, SEO, landing page, content, maintenance
rule: Website planning and maintenance are expensed. Application and infrastructure development may be capitalized if they create a controlled resource and meet software/intangible criteria. Content creation and advertising content are normally expensed unless specific asset criteria are met.
text:
Standard: IAS 38 / ASC 720, Paragraph: 350-40-25 / 38-69, Topic: Website Development and Hosting Costs
Rule: Website planning and maintenance are expensed. Application and infrastructure development may be capitalized if they create a controlled resource and meet software/intangible criteria. Content creation and advertising content are normally expensed unless specific asset criteria are met.
Keywords: website, web development, hosting, domain, SEO, landing page, content, maintenance

keywords: media buy, ad placement, insertion order, campaign schedule, prepaid advertising, billboard, online ads
rule: Payments for future advertising placements are recorded as prepaid advertising until the advertisement runs. Once the advertisement is aired, published, displayed, or delivered, expense is recognized.
text:
Standard: ASC 720 / IAS 38, Paragraph: ASC 720-35 / IAS 38.69, Topic: Advertising Prepayments and Media Buys
Rule: Payments for future advertising placements are recorded as prepaid advertising until the advertisement runs. Once the advertisement is aired, published, displayed, or delivered, expense is recognized.
Keywords: media buy, ad placement, insertion order, campaign schedule, prepaid advertising, billboard, online ads

keywords: legal fees, lawyer, attorney, audit fee, tax advice, professional services, consultant
rule: Legal, audit, tax advisory, consulting, and professional fees are expensed as services are rendered unless directly attributable to a qualifying asset, debt issuance, equity issuance, or business combination treatment.
text:
Standard: ASC 720, Paragraph: 25-1, Topic: Legal and Professional Fees
Rule: Legal, audit, tax advisory, consulting, and professional fees are expensed as services are rendered unless directly attributable to a qualifying asset, debt issuance, equity issuance, or business combination treatment.
Keywords: legal fees, lawyer, attorney, audit fee, tax advice, professional services, consultant

keywords: debt issuance cost, equity issuance cost, IPO cost, financing fee, underwriting, loan fee
rule: Debt issuance costs are generally deferred and amortized using the effective interest method. Equity issuance costs directly attributable to issuing equity are deducted from equity proceeds if offering is successful. Aborted offering costs are expensed.
text:
Standard: ASC 340 / IAS 32 / ASC 835, Paragraph: ASC 340-10 / IAS 32.37, Topic: Debt and Equity Issuance Costs
Rule: Debt issuance costs are generally deferred and amortized using the effective interest method. Equity issuance costs directly attributable to issuing equity are deducted from equity proceeds if offering is successful. Aborted offering costs are expensed.
Keywords: debt issuance cost, equity issuance cost, IPO cost, financing fee, underwriting, loan fee

keywords: dividend, distribution, retained earnings, shareholder payment, declared dividend, equity
rule: Dividends are recognized as a liability when authorized and no longer at entity discretion. Dividends are distributions of equity, not expenses.
text:
Standard: IAS 32 / ASC 505, Paragraph: IAS 32.35 / ASC 505-10, Topic: Dividends and Distributions
Rule: Dividends are recognized as a liability when authorized and no longer at entity discretion. Dividends are distributions of equity, not expenses.
Keywords: dividend, distribution, retained earnings, shareholder payment, declared dividend, equity

topic: Vendor Rebates, Discounts, and Purchase Credits
keywords: vendor rebate, purchase discount, supplier credit, credit memo, volume rebate, allowance
rule: Vendor rebates and purchase discounts reduce the cost of related inventory, asset, or expense when linked to a purchase. If underlying item has been sold or consumed, reduce COGS or expense. Do not record purchase rebates as revenue unless they are for distinct services provided to vendor.
text:
Standard: ASC 705 / IAS 2 / IAS 16, Paragraph: ASC 705-20 / IAS 2.11, Topic: Vendor Rebates, Discounts, and Purchase Credits
Rule: Vendor rebates and purchase discounts reduce the cost of related inventory, asset, or expense when linked to a purchase. If underlying item has been sold or consumed, reduce COGS or expense. Do not record purchase rebates as revenue unless they are for distinct services provided to vendor.

keywords: freight, shipping, delivery, courier, logistics, DHL, FedEx, UPS, inbound, outbound
rule: Freight-in, import duties, and handling required to bring inventory to its present location and condition are included in inventory cost. Freight-out or shipping to customers is a selling or fulfillment expense unless a separate shipping performance obligation exists.
text:
Standard: IAS 2 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 2.11 / ASC 330, Topic: Freight-In vs Freight-Out
Rule: Freight-in, import duties, and handling required to bring inventory to its present location and condition are included in inventory cost. Freight-out or shipping to customers is a selling or fulfillment expense unless a separate shipping performance obligation exists.
Keywords: freight, shipping, delivery, courier, logistics, DHL, FedEx, UPS, inbound, outbound

keywords: import duty, customs, tariff, landed cost, non-refundable tax, recoverable VAT
rule: Import duties and non-refundable purchase taxes are included in cost of inventory or fixed assets when directly attributable to acquisition. Recoverable VAT/GST is recorded separately as receivable.
text:
Standard: IAS 16 / IAS 2 / ASC 360 / ASC 330, Paragraph: IAS 16.16 / IAS 2.11, Topic: Import Duties and Non-Refundable Taxes
Rule: Import duties and non-refundable purchase taxes are included in cost of inventory or fixed assets when directly attributable to acquisition. Recoverable VAT/GST is recorded separately as receivable.
Keywords: import duty, customs, tariff, landed cost, non-refundable tax, recoverable VAT

keywords: travel, flight, hotel, accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxi, transport, airfare
rule: Business travel costs are expensed when travel occurs. Advance payments for future travel may be prepaid until travel date. Meals and entertainment require business purpose documentation and may have tax deductibility limits that do not change book expense classification.
text:
Standard: ASC 720, Paragraph: 25-1, Topic: Travel, Meals, and Entertainment
Rule: Business travel costs are expensed when travel occurs. Advance payments for future travel may be prepaid until travel date. Meals and entertainment require business purpose documentation and may have tax deductibility limits that do not change book expense classification.
Keywords: travel, flight, hotel, accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxi, transport, airfare

keywords: reimbursement, expense claim, employee payable, receipt, corporate card, out of pocket
rule: Approved employee reimbursements are recognized in the appropriate expense category based on underlying item and period incurred, not as generic payroll unless policy requires. Amounts owed to employees are employee payables.
text:
Standard: ASC 720, Paragraph: 25-1, Topic: Employee Expense Reimbursements
Rule: Approved employee reimbursements are recognized in the appropriate expense category based on underlying item and period incurred, not as generic payroll unless policy requires. Amounts owed to employees are employee payables.
Keywords: reimbursement, expense claim, employee payable, receipt, corporate card, out of pocket

topic: Bank Fees and Merchant Processing Fees
keywords: bank fee, wire fee, merchant fee, card processing, Stripe, PayPal, transaction fee
rule: Bank service charges, merchant processing fees, wire fees, and card fees are generally expensed as incurred. Fees directly attributable to debt issuance may be deferred under debt guidance.
text:
Standard: ASC 720, Paragraph: 25-1, Topic: Bank Fees and Merchant Processing Fees
Rule: Bank service charges, merchant processing fees, wire fees, and card fees are generally expensed as incurred. Fees directly attributable to debt issuance may be deferred under debt guidance.
Keywords: bank fee, wire fee, merchant fee, card processing, Stripe, PayPal, transaction fee

keywords: customer deposit, advance payment, prepayment, deferred revenue, unearned revenue
rule: Cash received from customers before goods or services are delivered is a liability, not revenue, until performance obligations are satisfied or refund obligation expires.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 210, Paragraph: IAS 1.54 / ASC 210, Topic: Customer Deposits and Advance Payments
Rule: Cash received from customers before goods or services are delivered is a liability, not revenue, until performance obligations are satisfied or refund obligation expires.
Keywords: customer deposit, advance payment, prepayment, deferred revenue, unearned revenue

keywords: accrued expense, accounts payable, invoice received, received not invoiced, GRNI, accrual reversal
rule: Use accounts payable when invoice has been received and obligation is recorded. Use accrued expenses when goods or services have been received but invoice has not yet been received or processed.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 405, Paragraph: 66, Topic: Accrued Expenses vs Accounts Payable
Rule: Use accounts payable when invoice has been received and obligation is recorded. Use accrued expenses when goods or services have been received but invoice has not yet been received or processed.
Keywords: accrued expense, accounts payable, invoice received, received not invoiced, GRNI, accrual reversal

keywords: prepaid, advance payment, future period, amortization, service period, subscription, insurance, rent
rule: Payments for goods or services to be received in future periods are recorded as prepaid assets and expensed systematically over the period of benefit. Immaterial prepaids may be expensed immediately if policy allows.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 210, Paragraph: IAS 1.66, Topic: Prepaid Expenses
Rule: Payments for goods or services to be received in future periods are recorded as prepaid assets and expensed systematically over the period of benefit. Immaterial prepaids may be expensed immediately if policy allows.
Keywords: prepaid, advance payment, future period, amortization, service period, subscription, insurance, rent

topic: Deposits Paid to Vendors and Landlords
keywords: deposit, security deposit, landlord deposit, refundable, non-refundable, retainer, advance
rule: Refundable deposits paid to vendors, landlords, utilities, or service providers are assets, not expenses. Non-refundable deposits are prepaid expenses or asset costs depending on purpose and period of benefit.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 210, Paragraph: 66, Topic: Deposits Paid to Vendors and Landlords
Rule: Refundable deposits paid to vendors, landlords, utilities, or service providers are assets, not expenses. Non-refundable deposits are prepaid expenses or asset costs depending on purpose and period of benefit.
Keywords: deposit, security deposit, landlord deposit, refundable, non-refundable, retainer, advance

keywords: restructuring, exit cost, severance, termination benefit, closure, relocation, redundancy
rule: Restructuring provisions are recognized only when detailed criteria are met. Under IFRS, a constructive obligation may arise from a detailed formal plan and valid expectation. Under US GAAP, one-time termination benefits and exit costs have specific recognition timing.
text:
Standard: IAS 37 / ASC 420, Paragraph: IAS 37.70-83 / ASC 420-10, Topic: Restructuring Costs and Exit Activities
Rule: Restructuring provisions are recognized only when detailed criteria are met. Under IFRS, a constructive obligation may arise from a detailed formal plan and valid expectation. Under US GAAP, one-time termination benefits and exit costs have specific recognition timing.
Keywords: restructuring, exit cost, severance, termination benefit, closure, relocation, redundancy

keywords: fine, penalty, settlement, regulator, legal settlement, violation, non-deductible
rule: Fines and penalties are expensed when incurred or when obligation is probable and estimable. Legal settlements follow provision/contingency guidance. Fines and penalties should be separately identifiable because they may be non-deductible for tax.
text:
Standard: ASC 720, Paragraph: 25-1, Topic: Fines, Penalties, and Settlements
Rule: Fines and penalties are expensed when incurred or when obligation is probable and estimable. Legal settlements follow provision/contingency guidance. Fines and penalties should be separately identifiable because they may be non-deductible for tax.
Keywords: fine, penalty, settlement, regulator, legal settlement, violation, non-deductible

Standard: ISA 240 / PCAOB AS 2401, Paragraph: ISA 240 / AS 2401, Topic: Fraud Risk - Revenue Recognition
Rule: Revenue recognition is presumed to be a fraud risk in audits unless rebutted. Audit AI should flag unusual revenue entries, manual postings, cut-off anomalies, side agreements, round amounts, and transactions near period-end.
Keywords: fraud risk, revenue recognition, cut-off, manual journal, side agreement, channel stuffing, quarter end

keywords: management override, manual journal, top-side, late entry, round amount, unsupported, post-close
rule: Manual journal entries, top-side adjustments, changes to estimates, and unusual transactions outside normal processes require review for management override risk.
text:
Standard: ISA 240 / PCAOB AS 2401, Paragraph: ISA 240 / AS 2401, Topic: Management Override of Controls

keywords: risk assessment, significant account, materiality, audit planning, inherent risk, control risk
rule: Accounts with high volume, complexity, estimation uncertainty, fraud susceptibility, related-party activity, or material balance should be flagged as significant accounts for audit planning and RAG retrieval priority.
text:
Standard: ISA 315 / PCAOB AS 2110, Paragraph: ISA 315 / AS 2110, Topic: Risk Assessment and Significant Accounts
Rule: Accounts with high volume, complexity, estimation uncertainty, fraud susceptibility, related-party activity, or material balance should be flagged as significant accounts for audit planning and RAG retrieval priority.
Keywords: risk assessment, significant account, materiality, audit planning, inherent risk, control risk

keywords: audit evidence, reliability, external evidence, confirmation, support, source document
rule: Audit evidence is more reliable when obtained from independent external sources, generated directly by the auditor, or supported by effective controls. Internally generated evidence alone is weaker, especially for high-risk estimates or related-party transactions.
text:
Standard: ISA 500 / PCAOB AS 1105, Paragraph: ISA 500 / AS 1105, Topic: Audit Evidence Reliability
Rule: Audit evidence is more reliable when obtained from independent external sources, generated directly by the auditor, or supported by effective controls. Internally generated evidence alone is weaker, especially for high-risk estimates or related-party transactions.
Keywords: audit evidence, reliability, external evidence, confirmation, support, source document

keywords: analytical procedure, variance, fluctuation, trend, margin, ratio, anomaly
rule: Unexpected relationships, unusual trends, margin changes, account spikes, or deviations from budget/prior period should be flagged for investigation. Analytical procedures support risk assessment and substantive testing but require corroboration for significant risks.
text:
Standard: ISA 520 / PCAOB AS 2305, Paragraph: ISA 520 / AS 2305, Topic: Analytical Procedures and Fluctuation Review
Rule: Unexpected relationships, unusual trends, margin changes, account spikes, or deviations from budget/prior period should be flagged for investigation. Analytical procedures support risk assessment and substantive testing but require corroboration for significant risks.
Keywords: analytical procedure, variance, fluctuation, trend, margin, ratio, anomaly

keywords: subsequent payment, search for unrecorded liabilities, SURL, AP cutoff, post year-end payment
rule: Payments made after period-end can provide evidence that liabilities existed at period-end. Post-period cash disbursement testing helps identify unrecorded liabilities and cut-off errors.
text:
Standard: ISA 560 / ASC 855, Paragraph: 560-12-855-10, Topic: Subsequent Payments as Audit Evidence
Rule: Payments made after period-end can provide evidence that liabilities existed at period-end. Post-period cash disbursement testing helps identify unrecorded liabilities and cut-off errors.
Keywords: subsequent payment, search for unrecorded liabilities, SURL, AP cutoff, post year-end payment

keywords: suspense, clearing, miscellaneous, uncategorized, unknown vendor, reclass, unresolved
rule: Suspense, clearing, miscellaneous, and uncategorized accounts should be temporary and regularly reconciled. Items must be reclassified to correct account once nature is known.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 210 / Audit Practice, Paragraph: 117-129, Topic: Suspense, Clearing, and Miscellaneous Accounts
Rule: Suspense, clearing, miscellaneous, and uncategorized accounts should be temporary and regularly reconciled. Items must be reclassified to correct account once nature is known.
Keywords: suspense, clearing, miscellaneous, uncategorized, unknown vendor, reclass, unresolved

topic: Offsetting Assets, Liabilities, Income, and Expenses
keywords: offsetting, netting, gross presentation, right of setoff, net settlement
rule: Assets and liabilities or income and expenses are not offset unless required or permitted by a specific standard and legally enforceable right and net settlement intention exist where applicable.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 210, Paragraph: IAS 1.32 / ASC 210-20, Topic: Offsetting Assets, Liabilities, Income, and Expenses
Rule: Assets and liabilities or income and expenses are not offset unless required or permitted by a specific standard and legally enforceable right and net settlement intention exist where applicable.
Keywords: offsetting, netting, gross presentation, right of setoff, net settlement

keywords: duplicate invoice, duplicate payment, invoice number, AP duplicate, fuzzy match, vendor duplicate
rule: Potential duplicate invoices should be held for review before payment or posting when vendor, invoice number, date, amount, bank account, PO, or description match prior transactions. Accounting classification is secondary until duplicate risk is resolved.
text:
Standard: Audit Practice, Paragraph: AP-DUP-01, Topic: Duplicate Invoice Detection
Rule: Potential duplicate invoices should be held for review before payment or posting when vendor, invoice number, date, amount, bank account, PO, or description match prior transactions. Accounting classification is secondary until duplicate risk is resolved.
Keywords: duplicate invoice, duplicate payment, invoice number, AP duplicate, fuzzy match, vendor duplicate

text:
Standard: ASC 850 / IAS 24 / Audit Practice, Paragraph: ASC 850-10 / IAS 24, Topic: Vendor Master and Related Party Audit Red Flags
Rule: New vendors, changes to bank details, vendors with employee addresses, duplicate tax IDs, and related-party links require enhanced review. Classification should be suspended or flagged if vendor legitimacy is not established.

text:

Rule: GL classification should include cost center or department based on who consumes the benefit, not simply who approved invoice. Shared costs should be allocated using a consistent, supportable basis.

keywords: materiality, threshold, capitalization policy, posting threshold, trivial, aggregate misstatement
rule: Classification decisions should consider quantitative and qualitative materiality. Immaterial items may be expensed under policy, but intentional misclassification to manage earnings is not acceptable even if individual items are small.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 720 / Audit Practice, Paragraph: 29-31, Topic: Materiality and Posting Thresholds
Rule: Classification decisions should consider quantitative and qualitative materiality. Immaterial items may be expensed under policy, but intentional misclassification to manage earnings is not acceptable even if individual items are small.
Keywords: materiality, threshold, capitalization policy, posting threshold, trivial, aggregate misstatement

text:

keywords: negative expense, credit balance, refund, rebate, reversal, vendor credit, expense reduction
rule: Negative expense balances and credit balances in expense accounts require review. They may be valid due to refunds, rebates, reclasses, or accrual reversals, but should be supported and classified correctly.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 720 / Audit Practice, Paragraph: 104, Topic: Negative Expenses and Credit Balances
Rule: Negative expense balances and credit balances in expense accounts require review. They may be valid due to refunds, rebates, reclasses, or accrual reversals, but should be supported and classified correctly.
Keywords: negative expense, credit balance, refund, rebate, reversal, vendor credit, expense reduction

keywords: aged payable, liability release, derecognition, write back, stale AP, extinguishment
rule: A liability is derecognized only when extinguished, paid, legally released, or expired under applicable law. Old payables should not be released to income solely because they are aged.
text:
Standard: IAS 37 / ASC 405, Paragraph: 37-79-405-20, Topic: Liability Derecognition and Aged Payables
Rule: A liability is derecognized only when extinguished, paid, legally released, or expired under applicable law. Old payables should not be released to income solely because they are aged.
Keywords: aged payable, liability release, derecognition, write back, stale AP, extinguishment

keywords: purchase order, commitment, open PO, executory contract, noncancelable, goods received
rule: A purchase order alone usually does not create an accounting liability until goods/services are received or an unavoidable obligation exists. Open purchase commitments may require disclosure if material.
text:
Standard: IAS 1 / ASC 720 / Audit Practice, Paragraph: 114, Topic: Purchase Order Commitments
Rule: A purchase order alone usually does not create an accounting liability until goods/services are received or an unavoidable obligation exists. Open purchase commitments may require disclosure if material.
Keywords: purchase order, commitment, open PO, executory contract, noncancelable, goods received

keywords: three way match, PO, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice match, receiving, GRNI

text:

Rule: Inventory and fixed asset purchases should be matched to purchase order, receiving evidence, and vendor invoice before posting or payment. Service purchases should be matched to contract/SOW and service acceptance.
Keywords: three way match, PO, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice match, receiving, GRNI
